title: Ready-state cell-window computation
statement: Let $Q,T$ have decidable equality, let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\iota:\mathrm{Fin}(3)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Fin}(k)$ be an embedding. Let $ws$ be a Boolean word and $s\in\mathbb{N}$ whose binary value is $s$. Suppose a $k$-tape configuration $d$ on the input obtained by embedding each Boolean symbol into the digit-symbol alphabet starts in the specified initial sweep state. On the three embedded tapes, tape 0 stores the digit encoding of $ws$ as a buffer relative to its head, while tapes 1 and 2 are blank everywhere. Then there is a time $t\le18(s+|ws|)+32$ such that the designated done state is not reached before time $t$, every head stays within distance $2s+|ws|+3$ of its initial position through time $t$, and at time $t$ the designated state is reached. At that time, the configuration is unchanged except that tape $\iota(1)$ contains, from its initial head position through the next $2s$ cells, a buffer of $s$ false cell symbols, one true cell symbol, and $s$ false cell symbols.
hypotheses_covered: configuration $d$ has the specified initial sweep state
for each three-tape index $i$ and integer position $p$, its embedded tape has the digit-buffer contents if $i=0$, and is blank otherwise
